findings.title: Written claim, extended consequence
findings.claim: The focus's speech is promised a written record and its speaker an extension of punishment. In the wider wealth boast at 18:34, the near-exact record-and-punishment sequence at 3:181, and the time-to-punishment relations at 19:75 and 3:178, the anticipated future becomes accountable and extension no longer reads as secure favor.
findings.mechanism: The carrier at 19:79:4:1 is the man's saying, and 19:79:2:2 makes that speech the object of writing. The independent boast at 18:34 supplies a wider wealth-and-offspring claim; 3:181 repeats writing what claimants said before naming punishment. The focus's punishment and extension then meet 19:75's respite until promised punishment and 3:178's respite that increases sin, changing the expected future into a written liability with an extended consequence.
findings.reader_payoff: A wealth boast becomes something preserved for account, while more time can lead into rather than away from consequence.
findings.containment: The focus still says that his speech will be written and punishment extended for him. The wider parallels color that wording but do not supply the focus's exact speech content or establish the object of inheritance or a solitary arrival at 19:80. The general extension facet remains distinct from the time-specific facet, which is carried by the contextual relation to 19:75 and 3:178.

epistemic.reason: The cross-run publication is marked trusted and focus word alignment is complete. The connection targets supply exact Arabic but no target morphology, and the duration reading depends on contextual parallels, so the wider relation remains qualified.

findings.title: Abundance as contested ownership
findings.claim: The focus's recorded saying meets a wider boast over wealth and offspring and the reminder that inheritance belongs to God; the expected abundance can therefore be heard as a claim under divine accounting rather than assured private ownership.
findings.mechanism: The carrier is the focus's saying at 19:79:4:1 and its promised writing at 19:79:2:2. The independent trigger at 18:34 supplies a comparable wealth-and-offspring boast, while 3:180 places hoarded wealth under burden and divine inheritance. Their contact with the focus's written account turns expected abundance into an accountable ownership claim.
findings.reader_payoff: The future wealth in a boast is no longer secure simply because it is claimed; it stands inside a record and a larger account of who inherits.
findings.containment: This keeps the focus's wording about recording what he says. It does not supply the exact content of that speech, state that the focus itself names wealth or offspring, identify the inheritance object at 19:80, or establish solitary arrival.

epistemic.reason: The HFT nomination is legacy_unbound and has no exact trace. The bounded contrast is independently supported by supplied 18:34 and 3:180 connection surfaces and returns through the focus's saying and writing relation.

findings.containment: The supplied parallels ground personal accounting only. They do not establish denied intercession, solitary arrival, or the full sequence described by the unbound summary, and they do not imply that others are absent from the surrounding scene.
